faith_group.name: Shintō Shrines
faith_group.title: Kannushi
faith_group.description: The kami are honoured at thousands of shrines across the islands. There is no national priesthood: each shrine answers to the kami enshrined there, and the kannushi who tend it answer to the local community.

faith_group.name: Rinzai Sect
faith_group.title: Rōshi
faith_group.description: The Rinzai Zen school is organised around the Gozan — the great Five Mountains — under abbots whose lineages descend from the Chinese masters of the Linji line. Daimyō patronise these monasteries openly.

faith_group.name: Sōtō Sect
faith_group.title: Zenji
faith_group.description: The Sōtō Zen school traces its line to Dōgen and Keizan, and its mother house Eiheiji sits in the snows of Echizen. Its abbots teach silent sitting before any other practice.

faith_group.name: Shingon Sect
faith_group.title: Daiajari
faith_group.description: The Shingon esoteric school keeps its high seat on Mount Kōya, where the founder Kūkai is said to wait in eternal meditation. Its great abbot transmits the Womb and Diamond mandalas to a chosen successor.

faith_group.name: Tendai Sect
faith_group.title: Zasu
faith_group.description: The Tendai school holds Mount Hiei outside the capital, and its head abbot — the Zasu — is one of the great religious lords of the realm. The school's warrior-monks have made and unmade emperors.

faith_group.name: Shin Sect
faith_group.title: Monshu
faith_group.description: The Jōdo Shinshū school is led hereditarily by the descendants of Shinran, whose Honganji line governs an unbroken community of lay believers across the central provinces. The Monshu's word can raise an army of farmers.
